pattern: failed to synthesize[\s\S]{0,200}(ContinuousSMul ℝ ℂ|IsBoundedSMul ℝ ℂ|NormSMulClass ℝ ℂ)
title: ContinuousSMul ℝ ℂ cannot be synthesized (competing Module ℝ ℂ path)
explanation: With `Mathlib.Algebra.Lie.OfAssociative` in the imports, `LieAlgebra.ofAssociativeAlgebra` supplies a second `Module ℝ ℂ` that is not defeq at instance transparency to the `NormedSpace` one. Then `ContinuousSMul ℝ ℂ`, and with it every `HasDerivAt (f : ℝ → ℂ)`, fails to elaborate, deterministically rather than by timeout.
fixes: Remove the instance locally: `attribute [-instance] LieAlgebra.ofAssociativeAlgebra` (the file does not use Lie algebras).
Or demote the projection: `attribute [local instance 10] LieAlgebra.toModule`.
Diagnose with `set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true in` on the failing line, and look for `LieAlgebra.toModule` in the trace.
example:
failed to synthesize
  ContinuousSMul ℝ ℂ

title: Exponent exceeds the exponentiation threshold
explanation: Lean refuses to evaluate `a ^ n` for literal `n` above `exponentiation.threshold` (default 256) during whnf or `decide`, so a numeric goal with large powers is left unevaluated.
fixes: Raise it for one declaration: `set_option exponentiation.threshold 1000 in` (vp-vnp does this in one file, and eth sets 2048 in its lakefile).
Avoid evaluation: rewrite with `pow_succ`, `pow_mul` or `Nat.pow_le_pow_right`, or use `norm_num`, which handles powers symbolically.
example: exponent 1600 exceeds the threshold 256, exponentiation operation was not evaluated, use `set_option exponentiation.threshold <num>` to set a new threshold

pattern: did not find (an )?instance of the pattern
title: rw does not find a pattern that looks identical (instance arguments differ)
explanation: The term in the goal and the left side of the lemma print the same, but their hidden instance arguments (for example `IsScalarTower ℝ ℂ ℂ`, or the `NormedSpace` inside `deriv` or `∫`) were synthesized along different paths, so syntactic matching fails.
fixes: Inspect with `set_option pp.explicit true in` to see the differing instances.
Use `erw`, `simp only [lemma]` or `convert lemma using 2`, which can unify up to instances.
If `set_option` is allowed: `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in` on the declaration, as zeta23 does in about 35 files (Mathlib's own workaround).
example:
tactic 'rewrite' failed, did not find instance of the pattern in the target expression
  deriv f x

title: Comparator mismatch on an auxiliary _proof_ constant
explanation: Elaboration creates auxiliary constants such as `Foo._proof_1` whose names and bodies depend on what was elaborated before. If the challenge copies only part of a definition layer, or uses other `open`s, these differ between challenge and solution, and the statement comparison fails although the definitions look identical.
fixes: Copy the definition layer completely, character for character and in the same order, with the same `open`s (zeta23 wraps it in an anonymous `section`).
In a nosorry submission, keep the given statement and its preceding definitions byte-identical, and put helpers after them, not between them.
example: constant Foo._proof_1 differs between challenge and solution

title: Section variables automatically included but unused
explanation: A theorem in a `variable` section does not use some instance or hypothesis variable that was still included. This is only a linter warning, but under `--wfail` or a no-warnings policy it fails the build.
fixes: Exclude it for that theorem: `omit [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] in theorem …` (vp-vnp does this).
Narrow the `section` or `variable` scope, or pass the argument explicitly.
As a last resort, `set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false` (vp-vnp sets it in about 196 files).
example:
automatically included section variable(s) unused in theorem `foo`:
  [Fintype ι]
